description: DAR-651: known-answer questions whose answer sits in a table, a figure or a scanned page. `pages` are 1-based PDF pages of `source` (the expected document), checked against the page images. kind: table = a table the current reader does extract, but split or with its caption apart from it; figure = text inside a drawing or picture; scan = a page that is an image of text, with no text layer. `indexed_chars` is what the committed index held for the page when the case was written.

cases.question: What is the maximum deflection of NC-PCB portable concrete barrier on concrete pavement at a 20 ft offset and a 60 mph design speed?
cases.answer: 25.37 in (impact angle 11.5 degrees), Figure 5, NC-PCB impact design table for concrete pavement
cases.note: The page-37 case: page 37 (asphalt, Figure 4) and page 38 (concrete, Figure 5) hold the same table layout with the same impact angles; each page's caption ends up in a chunk of its own, apart from the numbers.

cases.question: For NC-PCB on asphalt pavement, what maximum deflection does the design table give at a 44 ft offset and 70 mph?
cases.answer: 44.53 in (impact angle 12.7 degrees), Figure 4, NC-PCB impact design table for asphalt pavement

cases.question: What is the maximum vertical difference in elevation allowed between open lanes of traffic when the posted speed limit is 30 mph or more?
cases.answer: 2 inches; otherwise close one lane or provide a 6:1 slope between the lanes, and use Uneven Lanes (W8-11) signs

cases.question: On a roadway with curb and gutter, how close to an open travel lane can utility work be before the nearest travel lane must be closed?
cases.answer: Within 2 ft of an open travel lane: close the nearest open travel lane using Roadway Standard Drawing No. 1101.02 unless the work area is protected by barrier or guardrail

cases.question: What does a truck with a truck mounted attenuator need to weigh, and who decides if it is properly ballasted?
cases.answer: 10,000 to 20,000 lbs (truck and TMA, moving or stationary), ballasted by NCDOT approved methods; the Qualified Work Zone Supervisor determines if it is properly ballasted

cases.question: If a frac-out from directional drilling reaches the surface, how deep must the bentonite-contaminated material be removed?
cases.answer: By hand to a depth of 2 feet, contained and properly disposed of (Frac-out Contingency Plan, Attachment 24)

cases.question: When did NCDOT and DENR sign the Memorandum of Agreement on piping treated effluent within highway right of way?
cases.answer: January 25, 1999 (memo of November 15, 1999 to Division Engineers; addendum form)

cases.question: What spacing between advance warning signs A, B and C is recommended for utility work on an expressway or freeway?
cases.answer: A 1,000 ft, B 1,600 ft, C 2,600 ft (two-lane urban 200 ft each, standard 500 ft each)

cases.question: If the utility vehicle and work activity are 15 feet or more from the edge of the roadway, what traffic control is needed?
cases.answer: Only an activated flashing or revolving yellow light on the vehicle (Figure 10-4, work outside the shoulder)

cases.question: On what kind of street may the short layout with 200 ft sign spacing and a 50 to 100 ft taper be used for utility work, and where may it not?
cases.answer: Only low-volume, low-speed (35 mph or less) streets such as local residential streets; not in rural areas

cases.question: When ending guardrail on the trailing end of a rigid obstacle warrant to protect opposing traffic, how is L1 calculated?
How far before the intersection are tourist-oriented directional intersection approach signs placed, and where do advance signs go?
cases.answer: At least 200 ft before the intersection and 200 ft apart; advance signs at least 500 ft before, in special circumstances only (Figure 2K-2)

cases.question: What TODS county code does Onslow County have, and which division is it in?
cases.answer: County code 067, Division 3 (Form TOD-7, County List and Codes)

cases.question: For a 120 degree turn with an SU-40 design vehicle, what curve radius, offset and taper should the edge of traveled way use?
cases.answer: Simple curve radius with taper: 35 ft radius, 6.0 ft offset, 8:1 taper (Table 3, T-3)
cases.note: Table 3 runs over pages 19-22 with the same header on every page; the turn angle is printed only on the first row of each group.

cases.question: Is a traffic barrier required for a stream within the clear zone, and does the depth matter?
cases.answer: Yes if the stream or permanent body of water is more than 2 ft deep, no if less than 2 ft (Table 2, warrants for nontraversable hazards)
